simple.meaning: פִּתְגָּם (pithgâm) is a Hebrew word meaning “a (judicial) sentence.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פִּתְגָּם (H6599) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Esther 1:20, with occurrences in Esther, Ecclesiastes.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פִּתְגָּם (H6599) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פִּתְגָּם (H6599) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פִּתְגָּם (pithgâm) / H6599 is traced through Esther 1:20, Ecclesiastes 8:11 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6599. pithgam מִּתְגָּם noun masculine edict, decree (Persian loan-word, Old Persian patigâma ( patigam , come to, arrive ), New Persian paigâm , message ; see Gildem ZKM iv. 214 Mey Entstehung 23 ; Aramaic מִּתְגָּמָא , word, command , Biblical Aramaic = Biblical Hebrew); — construct ׳פ הַטֶּלֶךְ Est 1:20 ; with Genitive object ׳פ הָרָעָה מַעֲשֵׂה Eccl 8:11 (apparently f., compare De; but Hi Albr ZAW xvi (1896), 115 read נַעֲשֶׂה for נַעֲשָׂה ).

occurrences.englishText: When the king’s decree which he shall make is published throughout all his kingdom (for it is great), all the wives will give their husbands honor, both great and small.”
Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
